title: AI worsens climate change, integrated assessment shows
abstract: arXiv:2608.24670v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) interacts with climate in various ways, while a unified analytical framework of this intricate interplay is lacking. To align AI investment with climate policy, we propose such a framework integrating AI's impact on emissions, output, and climate damages into the DICE model. We distinguish between ICT-like and Industrial Revolution (IR)-like AI prospects. Calibrated to the best available evidence, we find that AI development is net polluting. Under current low abatement, ICT-like AI adds 0.1 degree C to 2100 warming, while IR-like AI adds 0.8 degree C. The associated climate costs offset roughly one-fifth and one-quarter of AI's economic gains, respectively. Meeting the 2 degree C target saves the optimal ICT(IR)-like AI investment rate by 2100 from 3.3% (5.1%) under the low-abatement scenario to 3.7% (12.7%), indicating that mitigation is complementary to AI development. tldr: 该论文通过整合AI对排放、产出和气候损害的影响到DICE模型，首次提出统一分析框架，发现AI发展是净污染的，且气候减缓政策与AI投资互补。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a unified framework integrating AI's impacts on emissions, output, and climate damages into the DICE model, finding that AI development is net polluting and that climate mitigation is complementary to AI investment.
